title: Dealing with locality in QAOA
abstract: Shallow-depth QAOA on sparse, high-diameter MaxCut instances faces a locality bottleneck: at depth \(p\), local observables can depend only on a bounded neighborhood of the circuit interaction graph. We propose a transport-augmented QAOA that keeps the MaxCut cost Hamiltonian unchanged but enriches the mixer with optimized, unweighted shortcut couplings (scheduled \(XX+YY\)) to collapse the effective interaction-graph diameter. Using exact finite-depth support recursions, we relate optimal shortcut placement to bounded-diameter graph augmentation, and show in benchmarks that (unlike ma-QAOA) performance becomes effectively size-invariant once the diameter is reduced. For bipartite families (base diameter 4), reducing the interaction path to \(d=1\) raises the ensemble-averaged approximation ratio from 0.7378 (ma-QAOA) to 0.9767 at \(p=1\) (\(σ=0.0251\), nine system sizes); on random trees (base diameter 10), at \(p=2\) it improves from 0.9226 to 0.9997 (\(σ=0.0001\)).
summary: This paper tackles the locality bottleneck in QAOA by proposing a transport-augmented mixer that adds 'shortcut' couplings to the circuit structure. Theoretically, this augmentation collapses the effective interaction graph diameter, which has been shown to remove depth-dependent constraints and significantly boost the algorithm's approximation ratio on sparse graphs.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is the 'locality bottleneck' in shallow-depth QAOA circuits when applied to sparse graphs with high interaction diameters.
main_result: By augmenting the mixer Hamiltonian with optimized shortcut couplings, the effective interaction graph diameter can be collapsed, leading to a significant and theoretically bounded improvement in the approximation ratio for MaxCut problems.
method: The authors use exact finite-depth support recursions and graph theory (diameter augmentation) to prove that reducing the circuit's effective interaction diameter removes depth-dependent locality obstructions.
model_or_system: The model is QAOA applied to finding the ground state of a MaxCut Hamiltonian on an instance graph G. The mixer is augmented by adding 'shortcut' couplings ($E_{new}$) to create a transport-augmented mixer, while the cost Hamiltonian remains fixed.
key_observables: Approximation Ratio (AR) for MaxCut; the support ($	ext{supp}$) of evolved observables, which is bounded by graph lightcones defined by the interaction diameter.
important_parameters: Circuit depth ($p$); base graph diameter ($	ext{diam}(G)$); the effective interaction-graph diameter ($d$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on establishing precise bounds on the support of evolved operators using commutator relations and lightcone criteria, assuming that the primary limitation is purely geometric/topological.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the Approximation Ratio for various graph types (bipartite, tree) showing a sharp increase towards unity when the interaction diameter is reduced to 1.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first identifying the locality bottleneck based on depth $p$ and graph distance. It then introduces the transport-augmented mixer using shortcut couplings. The core of the work involves deriving theoretical bounds (lightcone criteria) showing how these shortcuts collapse the effective diameter, leading to improved performance metrics.
why_interesting: The rigorous connection between graph topology (diameter) and quantum algorithm performance at finite depth is highly relevant for designing scalable quantum algorithms that overcome hardware connectivity limitations.
